key_insight: Automatic differentiation through a full compressible flow solver can map where sparse pressure data are most informative, revealing that aerodynamic information is transported unevenly and concentrated in localized high-observability regions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for choosing pressure sensor locations and improving inverse design or parameter identification in compressible aerodynamics.
method: Differentiable shock-capturing immersed-boundary solver for unsteady compressible flow
Backpropagate gradients through the simulation to define an observability metric
Use the metric to rank sensor locations and test inverse-learning performance
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-learning experiments across different flow regimes and airfoil geometries, comparing observability distributions and parameter-recovery convergence.
watch_item: High observability does not guarantee the best parameter recovery, so sensor selection must be validated against the specific inverse task and flow condition.
paper_title: Information Transport and Observability in Compressible Aerodynamics
